newsitem.title: UK: BT cuts charges for its internet services.
newsitem.headline: BT cuts charges for its internet services.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday it was cutting a range of charges for its mass market BT Internet service in what it hoped would be a boost to the growth rate of the dial-up computer access.

In a statement BT said its price cuts would take immediate effect and include a 20 percent cut in the monthly unlimited access subscription fee to 11.75 stg including tax, and a 50 percent cut in its ISDN high-speed link fee to the same price.
The service was introduced in March last year but BT said there was still a gap in the overall impact of internet useage in Britain.
"Our aim is to make quality Internet access as commonplace as the phone in the lounge," BT's multimedia services director Rupert Gavin was quoted as saying.
